text:
Carla: Quick proposal — move routing policy enforcement (priority, tenant-affinity, fallback order) into client libs (TS + Go) so the control plane can stop doing per-request enforcement. Should reduce p99 routing latency and cut backend QPS by ~15%.

Emily: Nice. How would we preserve telemetry for the console? We still need accurate counts for fallback + quota hits.

Carla: Plan is clients emit an opt-in header `X-RW-Client-Policy: v1` and a telemetry envelope we can ingest. Console will map that to a new column `client_policy` and a small tile for "client-enforced routing %".

Dave: Concern: this is a behavioural change in SDKs. Older clients will keep server-side enforcement. How do we avoid split-brain?

Carla: Server stays authoritative unless header present. Fallback path: if header absent server applies policy. That gives backward compatibility.

Ben: Product asks for rollout UX: we need a clear way for teams to see who is opted-in vs still on server. Also a rollback path if a client opt-in causes incorrect affinity.

Emily: Suggest phased rollout: 1) dark-launch header emission from newest SDKs (no enforcement), 2) ingest telemetry + console tile shows adoption, 3) enable client-side enforcement by default in SDK minor release behind a feature flag, 4) after adoption threshold (eg 80% of traffic from updated clients), flip server to prefer client header.

Dave: What about sampling? Emitting full per-request envelopes will blow up our metrics. Need sampling and a compact envelope.

Carla: Agreed. Proposal: clients send compact sampling header `X-RW-Policy-Sample: 1/100` and sampled payload via existing events pipeline. Non-sampled requests still include `X-RW-Client-Policy` boolean only.

Emily: Console mapping note: add two metrics — `client_policy_present_pct` (float) and `client_policy_sampled_events` (count). Show per-tenant and global view. Also expose a toggle to include/exclude sampled events in dashboard calculations.

Dave: SDK API suggestion (TS):
```ts
// opt-in when initializing client
new RedwoodClient({ enforceRouting: true, policyTelemetry: { sampleRate: 0.01 } })
```
Make sure `enforceRouting` default=false for one minor after release.

Carla: Good. For Go we mirror config. We also need a short-lived shim in the routing proxy to respect client header only for allowed tenants, and a kill-switch feature-flag if we detect affinity regressions.

Ben: Ops/Support needs a playbook entry: how to detect and roll back if clients cause affinity misrouting. Console should show a "policy health" badge (green/yellow/red) based on fallback spikes and SLA breaches.

Emily: Telemetry naming convention: `rw.client_policy.v1` for header, `rw.client_policy.sampled` for event lines. Keep names stable for future versions.

Dave: Breaking-change mitigation — we'll bump SDK minor and include migration docs with code snippets and test harness for tenant-affinity. We'll also add unit tests that assert header emission for common call patterns.

Carla: Rollout timeline proposal: week 0-2 dark-launch (telemetry only), week 3 release opt-in SDK minor, week 6 >50% adoption review, week 10 enable client-preference on server if safe.

Ben: +1. Add a customer-facing note in the Console release notes: "Client-side routing (opt-in) — benefits, telemetry, rollback steps".

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: posted canary job logs — canary v1.2.0-sdk-proxy-shim deployed to us-west-2 (3/3 healthy). :rocket:

Emily: I'll draft console tile mockups and telemetry docs. Carla, can you write the proxy shim spec and the kill-switch runbook?

Carla: Yep, I'll add a spec and link to the migration checklist.

Dave: We'll add an integration test in CI that spins up proxy+stub client with `enforceRouting=true` and verifies behaviour.

Ben: Thanks — this looks actionable. Please @eng-sre and @support once docs are up. :thumbsup:

Carla: tagging both when PRs land.

Emily: Marking this as RFC -> next steps: doc + UX mock + SDK PRs.

Dave: tiny FYI: watch for token refresh edge-case where client reauth causes loss of affinity headers. Add test coverage.

Carla: noted. Thanks all.
